PROVENANCE
Square-bracket annotations on leaves identify originating input-tree nodes. M = modular-tree (run 959850e3-81aa-4e37-a24a-8a32860cea1b); C = call-tree (a0075b75-ea50-4c2b-b7a1-13496ed95456); O = ownership-tree (938d0e94-1797-4078-a2f3-6acc3495c919); D = data-tree (6ff63464-5fa4-4cdf-916b-d287b395baf7).
M.A/S/P/T/R/F/I/C are the supplied lettered module nodes. C.init/key/clip/size/config/host/io/queue/read/render/search/close identify, respectively, Surface.init, keyCallback, clipboard completion, size/font entry points, updateConfig, main-thread dispatch, IO control loop, queueIo, PTY output loop, rendering loop, search loop and session closure. O.app/host/surface/state/io/worker/renderer/font/search identify CoreApp, runtime surface holders, Core Surface, renderer_state, Surface.io, io_thread, renderer, CoreApp.font_grid_set and optional search. D.T/G/F/W/X/H/L identify the supplied result nodes; D.C and D.U identify their nested effective-configuration and binding-resolution nodes. References to these nodes include their descendants. These aliases make each leaf's source and input provenance explicit without repeating entire tree paths.

CHECKED INTERSECTIONS
The following are literal cross-lens kernels supporting the selected concepts. Single-line input citations remain singleton slices; reading a larger function did not artificially increase intersection degree. Semantic corroboration with disjoint input citations can support a merged leaf without increasing its intersection degree.

C.read corroborates this activation, but its supplied citation is the documentation anchor at 702, not an overlapping slice.

REJECTED MERGES
Under I2, src/termio/Termio.zig:46-56 cannot establish ownership of the terminal: those fields are borrowed communication routes. Similarly, broad Surface.init coverage does not make the app-owned graphics device and surface-owned renderer one owner. The renderer update region contains image updates as well as snapshot capture; overlap there does not make image lifetime and snapshot completion one concept. Mutable Terminal and RenderState are also distinct despite both representing screen data: their relationship is a needs edge, not identity. These distinctions prevent large ancestor supports from manufacturing four-lens intersections.

STRUCTURE AND READING ORDER
The three canvases follow contracts and necessary coupling, not one default lens. First, Hosting and admission establishes runtime allocation, session lifetime and policy. Second, Transport and authoritative state separates asynchronous execution, application-aware VT interpretation and reusable emulator state. Third, Read models and presentation separates shared font/geometry services, terminal-derived read models and GPU scheduling/lifetime. Within each canvas, diagrams are ordered top-to-bottom. Named clusters distinguish public boundaries, retained state, hand-offs and teardown.
A module-only layout would hide mailbox and lock boundaries. A call-only pipeline would obscure shared resources and make search look synchronous. An ownership-only layout would bury the necessary dependencies of input encoding, geometry and snapshots. The chosen structure keeps those dependencies visible while merging repeated facts. Keyboard/paste and title reporting are representative paths; individual mouse gestures, clipboard protocols, Inspector widgets and shader passes are intentionally not expanded.

SOURCE CORRECTIONS AND QUALIFICATIONS
App.deleteSurface only unregisters; App.deinit nevertheless deinitializes remaining registered runtime surfaces before releasing shared resources (src/App.zig:136-150,220-240). A close request is not destruction: the embedded callback may even be absent (src/apprt/embedded.zig:678-685). Config ownership comments actually occur at src/Surface.zig:144-147. processOutput starts at 705, queueMessage at 437, and Termio.threadEnter at 367; supplied documentation anchors were not treated as function bodies. Parsing acquires the shared mutex, but blocking mailbox helpers can temporarily release/reacquire it (src/termio/stream_handler.zig:138-147); it is not an uninterrupted lock over every handler operation. Resize holds the same mutex across PTY notification and terminal resize, preventing child redraw from being parsed with old dimensions (src/termio/Termio.zig:534-553). endUpdate runs after terminal unlock and before snapshot consumption. Renderer CPU teardown closes the display link before thread handles disappear; GPU cleanup occurs on renderer thread exit. A short child run with exit code zero is not classified abnormal on non-Darwin platforms (src/Surface.zig:1303-1309). Reload changes terminal policy, not the running command/cwd. The POSIX reader includes a gather thread in addition to the IO and parser-reader threads.

RELATIONS AND FRONTIERS
All explicit endpoints are leaves; containment is expressed only by ASCII parenthood. calls edges naming mailboxes are asynchronous hand-offs, not synchronous stack calls. needs edges point from consumer to required input. owns expresses retention/replacement responsibility; depends expresses a component/service dependency. At coarser frontiers, lift endpoints to their covering ancestors, discard self-loops and merge parallel edges. Jump types, which the jump schema cannot store directly, are: session:7 -> transport:7 calls queued writes; admission:7 -> terminal:5 needs active input modes; admission:4 -> geometry:5 calls font replacement; interpreter:9 -> hosting:8 calls asynchronous host dispatch; readmodels:3 -> terminal:8 needs active screen storage; geometry:8 -> terminal:10 calls asynchronous resize through the coalescer.

DIMENSIONS
Produced 3 canvases versus target 3; diagrams per canvas 3/3/3 versus 3-4; intra-canvas edges 6/6/6 versus approximately 6. There are 6 unique jumps, incident counts 4/5/3 versus approximately 3 per canvas, averaging 4. This modest excess preserves both input-mode feedback and host-action feedback rather than hiding them to hit a count. The expanded graph has 59 leaves and 22 clusters. Maximum inclusion depth is 4 edges from the synthetic graph root, or 5 levels: root > canvas > diagram > cluster > leaf; ASCII trees themselves have depth 2. No maximum-depth target was specified. Diagrams are vertically separated by gaps exceeding their actual heights.
